page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a compute-focused cloud server from the Cloud Native product family. Hosted on KVM virtualization, it provides 12 shared vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. Memory capacity is configured at 24.0 GB, creating a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no local storage, requiring attached network volumes, and does not bundle dedicated GPU hardware or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent multi-threaded output alongside constrained single-core execution. The instance recorded 784.69 on the stress-ng single-core test, placing it in the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems, which reflects the lower clock frequency and shared CPU scheduling. Conversely, aggregate parallel execution achieves middle-tier results, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 11354.0 and stress-ng multi-core reaching 9386.85. Memory subsystem measurements show 60.68 GB/sec for large uncached read operations and 40.05 GB/sec for write streams. In workload-specific benchmarks, the server attained 16204.0 points in Geekbench Clang compilation and processed 17.86 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the shared AMD EPYC architecture offers access to a high core count without the capital cost of dedicated bare-metal allocations. A key technical tradeoff is the potential for compute latency variance under peak host activity, along with lower efficiency on serialized single-threaded tasks and unaccelerated large-model AI inference. The resource profile aligns with horizontally scalable, multi-threaded workloads including continuous integration build runners, distributed code compilation, ETL processing, and stateless microservice backends.
